old_caption: The video captures a serene yet dynamic scene at Niagara Falls. The camera is positioned close to the edge of the falls, providing an intimate view of the cascading water. The water flows vigorously over the rocky ledge, creating a misty spray that rises into the air, partially obscuring the distant trees and buildings on the horizon. The water's surface is turbulent, with waves and ripples reflecting the light, adding texture and movement to the scene. The mist from the falls diffuses the sunlight, casting a soft, ethereal glow over the entire landscape. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, allowing viewers to fully absorb the natural beauty and power of the falls. The overall atmosphere is one of tranquility and awe, inviting the viewer to appreciate the raw energy of nature.

caption: The video captures a wide, eye-level view of a waterfall crest, where a broad sheet of greenish-grey water moves steadily toward the right and tumbles over the lip into a bright, aerated curtain. A dark, flat-topped rock outcrop sits partly submerged in the lower-left foreground, remaining fixed while the surface around it ripples and deforms. Small standing waves and frothy patches shift along the crest, and the smaller cascade at the upper left churns with varying white water. Thick mist rises behind the falls, blurring the far shoreline and softening the pale, hazy sky. A line of bare trees is faintly visible along the top-left horizon, while drifting mist changes density across the background. The framing stays steady, emphasizing the ongoing flow of water over the edge. The water and mist keep moving within the fixed frame.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
